course.title: Hairdressing
course.tagline: Style, cut and care for women's hair: blowouts, treatments and salon-ready finishes.

days.title: Welcome to Hairdressing
days.goal: By the end of today you can explain and practise: Your kit is a dryer, round brushes, combs, clips, scissors, flat iron and heat protectant.

video.title: How to Do a Blowout

steps: Get your tools ready: round brush, hair dryer and flat iron.
Watch the video. It explains the main point in simple steps: Heat protectant must be applied before any hot tool touches hair.
Your kit is a dryer, round brushes, combs, clips, scissors, flat iron and heat protectant. Go slowly. Practise on a model or a practice head.
Do the same move three times. Check your work in a mirror or a photo after each try.
Write down what went well, what was hard, and one thing to do better tomorrow.
days.task: Practise welcome to hairdressing on a model or a practice head. Your kit is a dryer, round brushes, combs, clips, scissors, flat iron and heat protectant. Take a photo of your work.
days.challenge: Do welcome to hairdressing two times today. Make the second try neater than the first.

quiz.q: What is the key point of today's lesson on welcome to hairdressing?
options: You should rush through the technique to save time.
Heat protectant must be applied before any hot tool touches hair.
The best result comes from skipping the preparation step.
You never need to check your work until the very end.
quiz.explain: Heat protectant must be applied before any hot tool touches hair.

quiz.q: Which tool is most essential for welcome to hairdressing?
options: clipper with guards
trimmer
round brush
foil shaver
quiz.explain: The round brush is the essential tool for this work.

quiz.q: What should you always do when working on welcome to hairdressing?
options: disinfect your clippers between clients
never cut broken skin
check the client for cuts before starting
always use heat protectant before hot tools
quiz.explain: Always use heat protectant before hot tools.
